chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him)
That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) raced the cavalry horses and set the prize for their victory as an Awqiya of silver.

key_terms.أَجْرَى: To race or cause to run
key_terms.أَوَاقِيَّ: Awqiya (plural of Awqiyah, a unit of weight/money)

ai.seo_question: What was the prize for horse racing established by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the Prophetic tradition of maintaining military readiness through equestrian training, a practice highly valued in Shia jurisprudence for its role in jihad. By instituting silver awards for horse racing, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) not only encouraged physical prowess but also institutionalized material incentives to sustain the cavalry's preparedness for battle.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Giyad Bin Ibrahim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>
that Rasool-Allahsaww raced the cavalry horses, the first (prize) being an Awqiya (unit of measurement) of silver’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from abu ‘ Abd Allah, from his father, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn, recipients of divine supreme covenant, who has said the following: “

The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, made the reward for horse to race for a contest in the form of Awaqiy (a certain weight) of silver.”
